item.title: Packers Hall of Famer calls out AJ Hawk for silence during Aaron Rodgers’ McAfee rant
item.description: There is at least one former player who is defending Mike McCarthy , after several have reportedly confirmed the scathing allegations spewed by Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday afternoon. Rodgers went scorched earth on the Steelers’ head coach after his benching, and he has been backed up by unnamed players. One former player, Green Bay Packers Hall of Famer Greg Jennings, who won a Super Bowl in Green Bay under McCarthy, said he could not confirm any of what Rodgers claimed. He did, however, call out former teammate A.J. Hawk for just sitting around and not speaking up while Rodgers was making his claims on The Pat McAfee Show . Jennings wishes that Hawk would have been asked if he ever experienced what Rodgers was claiming, but instead, he sat in the shadows, as he’s been known to do on the show. MORE: Wildest Moments from Aaron Rodgers’ explosive Pat McAfee appearance Greg Jennings Wanted AJ Hawk To Speak Up Greg Jennings takes a shot at A.J. Hawk over Aaron Rodgers’ ‘McAfee Show’ interview: "A large part of me just wanted someone to ask A.J., who was sitting right there, do you recall any of this stuff?" 🏈 📺 🧀 https://t.co/TDCzKtxMIn — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 25, 2026 “I actually am surprised at a lot of it because there’s a lot that was said in this interview from Aaron that I, it overlapped my time in Green Bay, and I can’t bear witness to any of it. I was listening to it, and a large part of me just wanted anybody and someone to ask A.J., who was sitting right there, A.J., do you recall any of this stuff?,” Jennings said. “I’m like, please, someone ask A.J., can you confirm or can you second any of this? Because I couldn’t. And I’ve been texting with other teammates. They could. Now, I’m not saying that what he’s saying is not true, because I don’t think he sits up there and just embellishes to embellish. So I do believe that there is some truth to it. And Mike is going to have to, you know, correct it in his way and address it.” MORE: Mike McCarthy ice cream sandwich assistant becomes most famous man in Pittsburgh Jennings has a point, but at the same time, Hawk is always quiet on the show, and he attempts to get involved in controversy. If drama isn’t his thing, there’s no need to throw his name in the mix. The Rodgers-McCarthy saga isn’t going anywhere anytime soon, so the Packers great will be able to share his thoughts if he decides to, but for now, he’s fine just being an observer. item.description: (Talia Sprague-Imagn Images) Shortly after the Bears finished celebrating a 21-13 win – their fifth in a row – over the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, a group of coaches hustled back to Halas Hall that night to begin working on a plan for Thanksgiving Day in Detroit. “That’s got to be your catch-up time really, because you’re three days short of your normal prep time,” offensive coordinator Press Taylor said via Zoom on Monday. The Bears’ schedule has been anything but normal through the first 11 weeks of the season. The last Sunday-to-Sunday week came in the transition from Week 5 to Week 6. The next comes in Week 13 to Week 14. “It’s a quick transition right here (to Thursday),” Taylor said. “Now you’re trying to catch up on time and make sure you’ve got everything downloaded.” Here’s everything you need to know about the Bears in Week 12, from the podium to the locker room to the injury report. 1. Running back D’Andre Swift’s fumble issues are an obvious concern, but he still has the trust of the coaching staff. Swift did not receive another carry after his third lost fumble of the season against the Saints in the fourth quarter on Sunday. He received a similar punishment in Week 4 against the New York Jets after his second fumble of the year – also in the fourth quarter. “He just needs to hold on to the ball and we’ll be fine,” coach Ben Johnson said Tuesday. Swift’s three fumbles match his career high for a season, doing so in 2023 with the Philadelphia Eagles and 2020 – his rookie season – with the Lions. After each fumble and subsequent late-game benching this year, Swift has still received the start the following week. 2. Swift’s issues on Sunday opened the door for Salvon Ahmed off the practice squad, who’s made the most of his opportunities. Ahmed’s quick burst out of the backfield was noticeable in his limited action against the Saints. Among the Bears’ running backs in Week 11, his 19-yard carry was the largest gain out of the backfield. Thursday’s game marks his third and final allowable elevation from the practice squad to the Bears’ game-day roster. He will require a spot on the 53-man roster if the Bears want to use him beyond Week 12. That seems likely at this point. “He’s a guy that’s always flashed for us,” Johnson said. “He had a great preseason. I think we have a number of guys on the practice squad that are right on the edge of being able to contribute on game day for us. They’re just looking for an opportunity. He’s taking full advantage of his right now.” Ahmed could also factor into the Bears’ special teams plans, with running back Roschon Johnson unavailable for Thursday due to an ankle injury he sustained on Sunday. 3. Atlanta needs a shortstop and Chisholm has experience at the position. Reports have said that Chisholm is receiving interest in free agency from multiple teams. While Chisholm is seemingly a popular free agent , it remains to be seen if the Braves have any interest in him. Max Ralph of MLB.com recently addressed the idea of Atlanta pursuing the former Miami Marlin and New York Yankee. “Maybe you could squint to see a fit with Jazz Chisholm Jr., whose defense has been superb at second base over the past two seasons. Ralph was discussing potential options for the Braves shortstop uncertainty. While the writer clearly wasn’t suggesting that Atlanta needs to go all in on Chisholm at shortstop, the idea in itself is intriguing. While he likely wouldn’t be the shortstop of the long-term future, signing him to a multi-year deal could be an option for Atlanta. Chisholm could end up switching positions in the future if another shortstop candidate emerges on the roster. At the very least, Chisholm could help out at the position in 2027. With that being said, the Braves are not always among the biggest spenders in free agency. They may not have a desire to dish out a multi-year deal. If Atlanta is going to bring in a star to play shortstop, it will likely be through trade. Nevertheless, Jazz Chisholm Jr. is a free agent Atlanta could at least think about pursuing. item.title: Vincent Kompany calls on Bayern Munich to embrace the adversity, regain momentum after big loss to LOSC Lille
item.description: (Photo by S. Stingl/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images There is not a lot of room for positivity at Bayern Munich. The lead at the top of the Bundesliga table is gone, the Champions League top 8 looks like an impossible dream following the 2-1 loss to Lille OSC, the injury list is long and will not immediately improve, and — to top it all off — there has been needless drama around Jamal Musiala’s contract situation that has damaged the club’s image in the general public. But head coach Vincent Kompany knows not only that dwelling on the negativity never helps, but also the key to bringing back the positivity. “This is about momentum and fighting,” Kompany broke it down (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). “We simply have to get back to winning ways and then build on that, winning not just once, but twice, three times, four times, and get the machine runn ing again. There are no excuses. It’s simply the reality of the situation, and we have to stick together. Sometimes you have to enjoy the fight an d face the challenge head-on.” It really is that simple: Winning is the key. Kompany and the team will throw everything they have into improvin g and bagging a victory against Hamburger SV this weekend, buoyed not by any of the events of the past week, but by the knowledge that the only way to look is forward. item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 22: Cristian Javier #53 of the Houston Astros pitches during the second inning against the Seattle Mariners at T-Mobile Park on September 22, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. It also should not be lost on anyone that the Astros current options to fill out their starting rotation behind Hunter Brown all have various levels of risk. Options currently available to the #Astros on their 40-man roster for shaping their rotation: • Hunter Brown • Hayden Wesneski • Peter Lambert • Cristian Javier • Tatsuya Imai • Ethan Pecko • Ronel Blanco • Mike Burrows • Brandon Walter • Jackson Nezuh — Javier Gonzalez (@Astros_Coverage) November 22, 2026 Hayden Wesneski returned from Tommy John surgery last year and pitched very well in 11 starts. However he only threw 61 innings. Turning 29 in 10 days, he’s never thrown 90 innings in an MLB season. His durability to get through 33 starts, to maintain his production through 33 starts, and to produce as he did last season are all significant questions. Peter Lambert was a huge surprise for the team last season. At the MLB level, he set career highs in starts (29) and inning (155.2) and his 3.82 ERA is a number he had never previously approached (as evidenced by his career 5.32 ERA even after this past season). Entering his age 30 season, did the former 2nd round pick become a late bloomer or is a hard regression coming? How will his arm bounce back from a career high workload? Cristian Javier hasn’t looked the same since his phenomenal 2022 season. Since then, he has seen both a decrease and an inconsistency in velocity, he’s frequently had command issues, and he’s had Tommy John surgery. Last season wasn’t a pretty one for him, but his 1.96 ERA in September offered hope. Can Javier finally rebound at 30 years old, 5 seasons after his best work? Was September a breakthrough or an anomaly? Are his velocity issues a thing of the past? Can he rediscover his “invisiball” consistently? What is Javier at this point in his career? item.title: PSG held to draw in Champions League as Barcelona see off Sabah
item.description: Ousmane Dembele put Paris Saint-Germain ahead from the spot (Anne-Christine POUJOULAT) Paris Saint-Germain lost their perfect record in the Champions League as Roma held them to a 2-2 draw on Wednesday, while Anthony Gordon got a brace in Baku as Barcelona eased to victory over Sabah. Bayern Munich slipped to a 2-1 loss at Lille, further denting their hopes of an automatic last-16 berth via a top-eight finish in the league phase. Liverpool cruised to a 3-0 win at Club Brugge thanks to an Alexander Isak brace either side of a fine Florian Wirtz strike, while Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United were held to a frustrating 2-2 draw away to Sporting Lisbon. On a bitterly cold and wet night at the Parc des Princes, Donyell Malen's 17th goal in 16 matches this season denied Luis Enrique's twice defending champions as they failed to keep pace with Real Madrid, who are now the only remaining team with a 100 percent record in the competition. The Dutch forward's 78th-minute penalty ensured the sides finished level after Illia Zabarnyi's header and Ousmane Dembele's spot-kick had flipped the script for the hosts following Mario Hermoso's early opener for Roma. "It was the hardest match we have had this season and I am happy with the result," said PSG coach Luis Enrique. "I hope we don't have to play them later on over two legs." The result brought an end to a run of 12 consecutive wins for PSG, who have lost key attackers Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to injury recently, but they nonetheless look highly likely to secure a top-eight finish and avoid the play-off round, unlike in their last two campaigns. - 'No excuses' - A point further back than PSG lie Barcelona after Hansi Flick's charges showed no signs of missing Lamine Yamal as they beat Sabah 4-1. With the teenage star out with an ankle knock, England winger Gordon continued his love affair with the Azerbaijani capital. He scored twice either side of half-time to put Barca firmly in control, taking his tally in the city to six after he scored four goals in his previous appearance in Baku, against Qarabag for previous club Newcastle last season. "I've been very successful here," Gordon said. "Two goals, I'm happy with that. "A good performance, all in all, very good." Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus also found the net for the Spanish champions before Joy-Lance Mickels pulled one back for Champions League debutants Sabah. Bayern added a first defeat to their two wins and two draws so far in the competition as Vincent Kompany's injury-plagued side languish in 15th spot on eight points. "There are no excuses. item.title: FAMU women's basketball can't shake slow start in Kennesaw State loss
item.description: A 10-point first-quarter deficit ended up being the impetus for Florida A&M women’s basketball dropping its third straight game. On Tuesday, the Rattlers (1-5) lost their third straight game, 81-67, at Kennesaw State , played at VyStar Arena. The KSU Owls built a 24-14 end-of-first-quarter lead that FAMU couldn’t come back from. The remainder of the quarters were fairly even, but FAMU needed to make a run to cut into the deficit. FAMU shot 25-for-55 (45%) from the field, 3-for-10 (30%) from three, and 14-for-17 from the free-throw line (82%). The Owls went 27-for-55 (49%) from the field, 8-for-25 from beyond the arc (32%), and an impressive 19-for-20 from the charity stripe (95%). KSU narrowly won the rebounding battle 28-27 and had 17 turnovers compared to the Rattlers ’ 20. FAMU’s Niah Rhodes led the team with 20 points and contributed two rebounds and four assists. Kamryn Grant had 17 points and seven rebounds. Persais Williams scored 14 points, nabbed three boards, and stole the ball four times. All are guards. KSU was led by guards Shania Nichols, 28 points, four rebounds, two assists, two blocks, and two steals, and Kaelyn Flowers, 17 points, seven assists, and three steals. The Rattlers are back in action following the Thanksgiving holiday. They will travel to Stetson (2-6) on Dec. 1 to play in head coach Bridgette Gordon’s hometown. Tip-off is at 7 p.m. on ESPN+ from the Insight Credit Union Arena at Edmunds Center. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino fumes as Man United are “punished” in controversial Sporting draw
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino fumes as Man United are “punished” in controversial Sporting draw Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has hit out at the controversial referee calls that dearly cost his side in their dramatic 2-2 draw with Sporting CP. Controversy galore Pochettino’s wait for a first United win is set to continue following Wednesday’s draw with Sporting in Lisbon. The Red Devils were extremely hard done by as two major calls went their way, while goalkeeper Senne Lammens also endured a night to forget. Shortly before half-time, an Amad Diallo equaliser was ruled out by referee Szymon Marciniak owing to a foul committed by Youri Tielemans moments earlier. Marciniak permitted play to continue, but blew his whistle as Amad hit the crossbar, meaning that his finish seconds afterwards did not count. Replays plainly showed that Tielemans got the ball cleanly to set up Amad prior to pulling out of the challenge. Tielemans was also shown a yellow card for his troubles. Further controversy arose with ten minutes remaining as Suárez scored with an acrobatic finish after Lammens dropped the ball. United protested, but the goal stood for 2-2, and they subsequently had a goal of their own disallowed as the clock ticked down. It appeared that Kaique had scored an own goal, but after a VAR review, Patrick Dorgu was adjudged to have committed a foul on him, and the goal was chalked off. The decision appeared puzzling, given that Lammens had been subjected to equally minimal contact at the other end and Sporting’s goal was allowed to stand. To compound matters, Tielemans was shown a red card in the dying stages for a second bookable offence. item.title: MLB sues players union to boost lockout as deadline looms
item.description: Major League Baseball sued its players union in New York, hoping to secure protection from antitrust complaints in the wake of a lockout as a deadline looms to sign a new collective bargaining agreement (Mark Brown) Major League Baseball filed a lawsuit against the MLB Players Association on Wednesday seeking legal protection for a lockout expected to begin next week when their current collective bargaining agreement expires. The complaint filed in US District Court in New York seeks a declaration that a lockout would be legal under US antitrust law. The move would safeguard MLB if the players give up union status and try to sue MLB under antitrust law, exposing the league to potentially greater damages. MLB team owners have said they will not accept any new deal without a salary cap, a system the players union has successfully fought for decades. With a Tuesday deadline fast approaching, the lawsuit raised the stakes as both sides fought to determine how to divide billions of dollars in profits. "Today's filing is a defensive measure simply intended to keep the parties at the bargaining table to work towards a new collective bargaining agreement and a full 2027 season," MLB spokesperson Glen Caplin said. "We believe the union is preparing to follow the playbook its new leadership has used against other major professional sports leagues by pretending to 'disclaim' its status as the players' bargaining representative to pursue an antitrust lawsuit as an end run around the bargaining process. "We have asked a federal court in the Southern District of New York to proactively disarm the union's nuclear option of disclaiming." MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer called the lawsuit "completely frivolous" in a statement. "We will respond appropriately, but MLB's decision to run to court in the middle of negotiations rather than bargain in good faith is incredibly disappointing." js/pnb
